transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I came in because... well, for a really long time now, I just wake up already feeling low. It's like there’s this heavy, gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic for work, and it pretty much just follows me through the whole day.
Have you experienced similar periods of feeling this low in the past, perhaps months or years ago?

It's not really like it comes and goes, so it's not just in the past. It's been pretty constant. I've been feeling this way for about two years and two months now. It basically started ever since the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place.
During these past two years, have there been any periods of two months or longer where you felt like your mood was back to your normal baseline?

No, um... not at all. There hasn't been any break like that. Like I was saying, it's been pretty constant the whole time. I definitely haven't had a couple of months where I felt back to normal. It's just always there.
During these past two years, have you noticed a change in your appetite, such as eating significantly more or less than you used to?
No, I haven't really noticed any change with my appetite. I pretty much eat the same amount I always have.
Have you had any trouble with your sleep, such as difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much?
No, my sleep has been fine. I haven't really had any trouble falling asleep or anything like that. I just sleep my normal amount.
How would you describe the way you feel about yourself, or your level of self-confidence, during these past two years?

Um, I don't think my self-confidence has really changed. I feel okay about myself, honestly. I haven't noticed feeling worse about who I am or anything like that. It's just my overall mood that's the problem, not really how I view myself.
During these past two years, have you felt like you have had less energy than usual or that you are easily fatigued?

Yeah, definitely. I feel tired pretty much all the time. Even if I have a day off or I get to sleep late, my body still just feels completely worn out. By the time I finish work—you know, rooming patients and catching up on all the charts—it feels like I have absolutely nothing left in the tank. I don't even have the energy to do my laundry, go shoot hoops, or, um, even mess around with my electronics stuff.
During these past two years, have you often felt a sense of hopelessness about the future?

Yeah, I do. I just keep thinking that this is just how life is going to be now. Just working random hours, always falling behind... I don't see how I'm ever going to get enough money, or even the energy, to move forward with school or do anything better.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating on your tasks or making decisions over the past two years?

Yeah, it's been pretty hard to concentrate lately. Um, at work, I'll just be staring at a patient's intake screen, and I have to reread the same line over and over again before it actually registers. And... I don't know, I've caught myself missing little details, like medication doses, or I'll just completely mix up what I was about to ask the patient next. It's like my brain just won't focus.
Have you noticed that you have lost interest or pleasure in doing the things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still like the idea of playing basketball or tinkering with my electronics. It's not that I don't care about them anymore or don't want to do them... I just, like I said, I just don't have the energy for it. If I wasn't so tired all the time, I'd definitely still be doing all that stuff.
During these past two years, have you ever felt that life is not worth living or had thoughts of harming yourself?

No, I haven't really had thoughts like that. I mean, it gets really frustrating feeling so stuck and tired all the time, but... I don't want to hurt myself or anything. I don't think about dying. It's just hard getting through the days sometimes, but I've never felt like I wanted to end it.
